Thanks Sarah — we're on it.

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from first-pass dashboards: p95 and p99 for the hosted-api node pool spiked starting ~08:38 UTC. Concurrent in-flight request count jumped and queue depth increased sharply for the high-throughput routing policy. Initial hypothesis is that an increase in client concurrency combined with dynamic batching window growth caused oversized batches and slowed per-request latency (prefetch/backpressure on GPU queues).

Dylan — can you pull the queue depth and batch size histograms for the 08:20–09:10 window? If batching window expanded we should see median batch size jump and a long tail. Also paste the routing-policy rollout status for the US pool — want to confirm we didn't accidentally shift more traffic to the single high-util node set.

Sarah — thanks for the logs. We'll keep you updated and propose a short mitigation (reduce dynamic batch window, temporarily pin to lower-batch routing policy) while we root cause.

I added a live dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/hosted-api/qdepth?range=2h

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 09:20 AM karthik.iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Dylan — can you pull the queue depth and batch size histograms for the 08:20–09:10 window?

Pulled graphs and a short dump (attached). Observations:
- At ~08:36 UTC concurrent requests into the US-hosted pool jumped ~3.6x due to a ramp from Fintegrate's client (their traces confirm a small spike in concurrent multiparallel requests).
- Dynamic batching window auto-adjusted upward to try to improve throughput; median batch size increased from 6->18, tail to 46. That caused head-of-line latency for small interactive requests and pushed P95/P99 up as batches queued on GPU.
- KV cache miss-rate for the model increased slightly (possible cold-start of a hot path), but the dominant signal is queue/backpressure.
- Autoscaler didn't immediately slice traffic across additional GPU groups because the routing policy held traffic to the "low-latency" pool; scaling was delayed by policy cooldown.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:27 UTC (done):
- Reduced dynamic batching window by 40% for the US pool (reduces oversized batch formation).
- Temporarily disabled strict routing-policy pinning so the load balancer can spread traffic across warm secondary nodes.
- Enabled fallback to the compatible smaller-quantized model for long-running batched requests (keeps interactive latency lower while preserving throughput).

Initial result: p95 improved from ~1.9s -> ~740ms within ~6 minutes; error rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.3%. P99 still elevated but trending down.

Attachments: queue_dump_20270403.png (queue depth/batch histograms)

I'll keep watching and will post a more complete RCA once we stabilize.

— Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

What we did (completed):
- Reduced dynamic batching window for the US-hosted pool (09:27 UTC).
- Relaxed strict routing-policy pin so autoscaler can spread load across additional warm nodes (09:29 UTC).
- Enabled fallback to compatible smaller-quantized model for batched jobs (09:31 UTC).

Immediate outcome: p95 dropped from ~1.9s -> ~740ms; error rate decreased from 1.8% -> 0.3% within ~6 minutes. P99 reduced but still slightly elevated — we're watching to ensure full tail recovery.

Next steps:
- We'll monitor for 2 hours. If p99 remains >1.5s after 90 minutes, we'll revert the routing-policy rollout and run a controlled autoscale (JIRA-INF-2120).
- I'll send a short incident note for your AE and CS team with timestamps and what changed.
- If you can share any additional traffic pattern changes on your side (client-side concurrency spike), that will help us prevent recurrence.

Thanks for flagging quickly and apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with priority.
